problem: H = NI/l is presented as a plain definition of field strength. It is only true for a uniform path. In this same chapter the worked example has an iron core plus an air gap, where H is different in the iron and in the air, so a student may wrongly compute H = 1000/0.401 = 2494 A/m for the whole circuit.
fix: Write: for a uniform section, H = F/l = NI/l in A/m. When the path has sections of different μ, H differs section by section and the MMF splits as H_c l_c + H_g l_g = NI.

problem: The forward reference 'treated in 4.5' is plain text, so the reader gets no clickable link to that chapter, unlike the linked cross-references used elsewhere in the book.
fix: Point to the inductance chapter as a link, e.g. 'see inductance from reluctance', and make sure the target chapter id matches.

problem: 'A coil on a core is a source of magnetic pressure' introduces a non-standard term (magnetic pressure) that is never defined and is not used again; it can be mistaken for a real quantity.
fix: Say directly: 'A coil on a core is the source of the magnetic flux. The magnetomotive force (MMF) it produces is F = NI.'
